cards.explanation: The answer is the nations the LORD drove out. Manasseh, Hezekiah's son and king of Judah, did evil by following the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites. Copying a neighbor's cookie recipe is one thing, friends. Copying the ways of nations God had already cleared out is something else entirely.

The answer is False. Verse 3 says Manasseh, king of Judah, rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed. All that tearing down, and the son put it right back up. It's like watching somebody un-bake a whole batch, friends.
The answer is altars. Verse 3 says Manasseh, king of Judah, raised up altars for Baal, a false god. He didn't just let the old places stand there, friends. He raised up new altars for Baal.

The answer is both of them. Verse 5 says that in both courtyards of the house of the LORD, Manasseh, king of Judah, built altars to all the host of heaven. Not one courtyard, but both. I think that's why the verse is so heavy.

The answer is mediums. Verse 6 says Manasseh, king of Judah, practiced sorcery and divination, and consulted mediums and spiritists. The text calls it great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger. I'll stick to asking the LORD, and a good oven timer, friends.

The answer is that they had to do all He commanded. The LORD says, “…if only they are careful to do all I have commanded them…” and then names the whole Law that His servant Moses, Israel's leader, commanded them (2 Kings 21:8). The promise came with a condition, friends. I'd never try a recipe and skip half the steps either.

The answer is True. Verse 9 says the people did not listen and Manasseh, king of Judah, led them astray. The king was out front and the people followed. When a leader heads off the road, a lot of folks end up in the ditch with him, friends.

The answer is that it's greater than theirs. Verse 9 says Manasseh, king of Judah, led the people astray, so that they did greater evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites. Greater than the very nations God had destroyed. That's a hard line to read, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says He is bringing such calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah that the news will reverberate in the ears of all who hear it (2 Kings 21:12). No peace and security in that message, friends. It's calamity.

The answer is bowl. In verse 13 God says He will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes out a bowl, wiping it and turning it upside down. I know that picture from my own mixing bowls, wiped clean to the last crumb and flipped over on the rack. It's a heavy picture, and God says it plainly, friends.

The answer is that He will deliver them to their enemies. Verse 14 says God will forsake the remnant of His inheritance and deliver them into the hands of their enemies. It's a hard thing to read, friends. I won't dress it up, because the text doesn't.

The answer is Egypt. Verse 15 says they have done evil in God's sight and provoked Him to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day. That's a long stretch of time, friends. The LORD is counting from the very beginning of their journey out.

The answer is in his palace garden. Verse 18 says Manasseh, king of Judah, rested with his fathers and was buried in his palace garden, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon reigned in his place. Verse 26 says Amon was buried in that garden too.

The answer is True. Verse 20 says Amon, Manasseh's son, did evil in the sight of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. Verse 21 says he walked in all the ways of his father. I wish it were different, friends.

The answer is idols. Verse 21 says Amon, king of Judah, walked in all the ways of his father, and he served and worshiped the idols his father had served. Those were the same idols his father had served. Like father, like son, and that's the sad part, friends.

The answer is his own servants. Verse 23 says the servants of Amon, king of Judah, conspired against him and killed the king in his palace. The plot came from the people closest to him. The text doesn't give a reason, so I won't make one up, friends.

The answer is his son Josiah. Verse 24 says the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place. Josiah is Amon's son. One more name to keep close, friends.
